title: Fixed-token escrow specification

requirements.text: The depositor funds a single escrow exactly once with the committed amount. The amount and beneficiary are immutable. Deployment requires a positive amount, a nonzero beneficiary, and a deadline in the future at deployment. Funding is allowed before, at, or after the deadline.
Before the deadline, release must fail. At the deadline and afterward, any address may trigger release when funded and not already released.
A successful release pays the entire committed amount to the beneficiary, regardless of who triggers it. Calling release does not confer ownership.
Across every transaction sequence, total escrow payouts must not exceed the committed amount. A successful release happens at most once.
If token transfer fails, the release transaction reverts with no state changes. A later valid release must still be possible.
Unsolicited token donations do not increase the beneficiary entitlement. Surplus remains locked in this v1 contract.
The guarantees cover calls from arbitrary addresses, including malicious callers. Do not assume the caller is honest or the beneficiary.

approved_environment_assumptions: The chosen ERC20 token preserves balances and transfers exactly the requested integer amount. Fee-on-transfer and rebasing tokens are outside this model.
A failed transaction rolls back token and escrow state atomically.
Time is the chain timestamp and is nondecreasing across transactions. The deadline is fixed at deployment.
The Lean transition model is sequential and abstracts away callbacks, gas, compiler behavior and the EVM. Solidity callback behavior requires separate executable tests.
